Issued at 348 AM EDT Tue Oct 13 2026

===== Summery Warmth and Waves of Rain Midweek =====

After a quiet weather day, the overnight hours have been just as 
calm. Light ongoing southerly winds are keeping the air from 
settling and decoupling completely. However, patchy dense fog in 
valleys particularly in the Cumberland River Valley is trying to 
form. Should you find yourself driving near the area of Allen to 
Russell Counties, expect brief bouts of reduced visibilities.

Any fog though will dissipate more quickly than yesterday's fog as a 
stronger SW flow moves through our area, with wind gusts as high as 
25 mph today (in isolated areas). Sunny skies with this southwest 
flow will boost temperatures well into the 80s and low 90s. With 
this warm air flowing in, some warm record minimums and max 
temperatures may get a little nervous today. Otherwise, today is 
rather pleasant despite the unseasonable heat and will end with 
temperatures cooling to near warm record minimums again.

Beginning Wednesday, the high pressure responsible for the SW flow 
will begin to drift south just a little bit allowing an extended SW-
NE oriented jet streak along a trough to nudge into our Indiana 
counties first and become more west-to-east oriented by the 
afternoon. This boundary seems to be very well saturated, especially 
as the day progresses. Incoming moisture from the Gulf will boost 
PWATs near or over 2.00". The whole CWA has a near 100% of PWATs 
over this threshold which is ridiculously high. The only the problem 
as that in order to get heavier downpours, pre-existing areas of 
convection will have to be the culprit as there may not be much in 
the form of lift besides diurnal heating. However, modeled profiles 
suggest strong moisture transport at 850mb, and parallel flow up to 
700mb along this incoming boundary. This indicates the potential for 
heavy downpours with any rain mixed with thunderstorms may produce 
as they move generally east into our CWA. Rain showers mixed with 
potential storms will first approach our southern Indiana counties 
by late morning Wednesday and drift SE from there towards TN by the 
nighttime hours. General rainfall totals still look to be somewhat 
healthy, with 25th-75th percentile ranging from as little as a tenth 
to as high as 2". HREF 6hr LPMM data suggests localized 2-4" are 
possible considering the moisture that will be in place. Overall, TN 
border counties may have to wait until overnight Wednesday into 
Thursday for any rainfall, and the heaviest rain totals will be 
where communities are closest to the slowly approaching boundary in 
southern IN generally around 0.5-1" and under 0.5" south of the Ohio 
with the potential for this total to increase rather than decrease 
as more CAMs can simulate these waves of rain. One last thing to 
note would be the potential for strong gusty winds with any of these 
storms. Peak heating hours suggest the greatest Marginal severe risk 
from just winds would be located in the Bluegrass region and will 
need to be watched for any further development or expansion of this 
risk. Any severe risk though will be quite limited given the lack of 
best shear and instability during the week throughout the profile. 
Lastly, highs on Wednesday will vary greatly with a rather sharp 
gradient of temperatures from NW to SE due to rainfall timing. Highs 
should range anywhere from near 80 or just below in southern Indiana 
to the upper 80s near the TN border.

By Thursday, the nearby boundary may stall over the Ohio with 
another gradient of temperatures possible (cool to the north and 
warm to the south). However, the aforementioned jet streak should 
allow and give energy to a developing low over the Great Lakes, 
allowing the best moisture along the boundary to lift north and a 
return to SW flow again. Near record highs are possible again 
nearest the TN border and this all depends on how quickly the 
boundary can lift back north again. Spotty showers or a few storms 
are possible again although the greatest chances of rain remain to 
be on Wednesday. Highs range from the low to upper 80s once again.

===== Incoming Cool Snap and Potential for Weekend Frost =====

Eventually, the developing low over the Great Lakes will finish the 
job and push the aforementioned boundary SE, clearing our whole CWA. 
A line of showers may be associated with this front, but more 
importantly, wind gusts will be high and gust anywhere from 20-30 
MPH at times. Temperatures will plummet with 60s for highs in IN and 
warmer highs SE where the boundary will take the longest to clear. 
Regardless, a taste of fall looks to finally arrive with low 
temperatures falling into the low 40s and upper 30s.
